name: Bass Guitar
shortDescription: Four-string electric bass providing low-frequency harmonic foundation through magnetic pickup induction.
description: The electric bass guitar occupies the low-frequency foundation of modern ensembles. With a longer scale length (~864mm) and heavier wound strings, it produces fundamentals from 41 Hz to 300 Hz. Split-coil or soapbar pickups transduce string vibration electromagnetically, while the solid body's mass contributes long sustain without acoustic resonance losses.
historicalOrigins: Invented by Leo Fender in 1951 as the Precision Bass, replacing the upright double bass in touring bands. The long neck and fretted fingerboard allowed precise intonation without the physical demands of the upright.
acousticPrinciples: Longer scale length (864mm vs 648mm) lowers fundamental frequency per Mersenne's law
Heavier wound strings (0.045–0.105") increase linear mass density μ, lowering pitch
Split-coil pickup humbucks 60 Hz noise while sensing both halves of string per string pair
Solid alder or ash body provides mass for sustain without acoustic resonance losses

characteristics.orchestralRole: Harmonic foundation, rhythmic pulse, groove anchor

soundDNA.exciter: Finger pluck or pick on heavy nickel-wound steel strings
soundDNA.resonator: Split-coil electromagnetic pickup + solid ash/alder body
soundDNA.attackDecay: Medium-fast attack (5–10ms), sustained fundamental with slower decay
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Thick, warm, punchy; finger style adds harmonic warmth

body.label: Solid Bass Body
body.function: Alder body provides mass for sustain. Contoured for ergonomic player comfort.

characteristics.material: Solid alder or ash with polyester finish
characteristics.mechanism: Mass sustain with minimal acoustic resonance

pickup.label: Split-Coil Pickup
pickup.function: Two-part humbucking pickup, each half sensing two strings. Cancels electromagnetic interference.

characteristics.material: Alnico V magnets with fibre-bobbin copper coil

bridge.label: Heavy Bass Bridge
bridge.function: High-mass bridge transfers string energy to body and allows intonation per string.

characteristics.material: Bent steel or cast zinc with chrome saddles

neck.label: Long-Scale Neck
neck.function: 34" (864mm) scale neck lowers pitch range. Truss rod counters 80–100 kg string tension.

characteristics.mechanism: Long rigid beam; scale length controls pitch
characteristics.role: Scale length and string tension support

fretboard.label: Maple Fretboard
fretboard.function: 20 frets providing semitone pitch quantization across 34" scale.

characteristics.material: Maple or rosewood with stainless-steel frets
characteristics.mechanism: Scale-length fret placement per equal temperament

strings.label: Heavy Wound Strings
strings.function: High-mass wound strings create low-frequency standing waves (41–392 Hz).

characteristics.mechanism: Transverse standing waves; high μ for low pitch

tuners.label: Tuning Machines
tuners.function: 4 sealed-gear tuning machines with 20:1 gear ratio for stable low-tension tuning.

followTheSound.title: Low-Frequency Vibration
followTheSound.explanation: Heavy wound string vibrates at 41–392 Hz, creating slow transverse waves.

followTheSound.title: Split-Coil Induction
followTheSound.explanation: Each split-coil half senses two strings, cancelling hum while preserving bass signal.

followTheSound.title: Body Mass Sustain
followTheSound.explanation: Solid body mass prevents energy loss, extending sustain without acoustic resonance.

followTheSound.title: String-Body Coupling
followTheSound.explanation: Bridge transfers remaining vibrational energy into the body for tonal colouration.
